item.title: Poland shooting leaves 6 dead and 16 wounded as minister calls it an 'act of terror'
item.description:
KRAKOW, Poland (AP) — Six people were killed and 16 wounded after a gunman opened fire Saturday afternoon in a busy market square in Krakow, authorities said, in what Poland ’s defense minister called an “act of terror” on the people of the city.

The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, opened fire with an automatic weapon in the city’s Main Square, a major tourist destination. He was fascinated with far-right ideologies and held “very radical" and “ultra-nationalistic" views, Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said at a news conference.

Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz called Saturday’s fatal shooting an “act of terror” on the people of Krakow, Poland's second-largest city, which receives 15 million visitors a year, most of them passing through the Main Square.

Four women and two men were killed. Two police officers were wounded, one seriously, Kierwiński said. Thirteen of the 16 people injured were brought to the hospital with serious injuries, and one of them was a foreign citizen.

It was not immediately clear how many of the victims had suffered gunshot wounds, though two people had already been released from medical treatment within hours of the attack.

People were wounded at several locations

The perpetrator was shot and wounded during a gunfight with officers a short distance away from the initial violence, police said. He was taken to the hospital for surgery.

Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Krakow police, said the perpetrator was wearing military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest and used a military-type long gun in the attack. Police found many other weapons, as well as ammunition, in his car. He kept firing at the police even after being shot himself, she said.

The attacker engaged in a “wild ride” around the Main Square, Cisło said, which is why people were wounded at several locations.

Cisło added that the gunman acted alone and that the public is safe.

Krakow mayor Łukasz Gibała said the city will be in official mourning until Wednesday. He vowed that Krakow will remain open to visitors despite the tragedy.

“The square will belong to us again,” Gibała said in a video posted to X.

Mass shootings are rare in Poland

Videos posted on social media by witnesses show people running away from the square to take cover on small streets nearby, as well as first responders trying to resuscitate victims. In one of the videos, a policeman is seen repeatedly shooting the attacker, who is lying on the street, only to later slowly collapse himself to the ground.

Photos showed a Polish Medical Air Rescue helicopter after it landed in the square.

It was not immediately clear whether the firearm used in Saturday’s attack, or the guns found in the perpetrator’s car, were legal. Around 411,000 people hold gun permits in Poland, which has a population of 37 million, and interest in gun ownership has been rising.

Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland. However, in mid-October three attacks at schools in the central province of Mazovia took place within four days, leaving one person dead and many wounded, including children.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, in a post on X, praised the police officers who responded to Saturday’s tragedy. Polish President Karol Nawrocki said his thoughts were with the victims, the wounded and their families.

A tram driver reported around 3 p.m. that his vehicle was shot at from a man in a moving car while passing nearby the main square, the Krakow municipal transport company said. The window to the tram driver’s cabin was shattered.

Animal rights group OTOZ Animals said the attacker also shot two horses. Both animals are alive, but one was grazed by a bullet and the other hit in the leg. White carriages drawn by horses are a main tourist attraction in the square.

Warsaw mayor Rafał Trzaskowski announced increased security measures, including road barriers, along main streets in the old town in the Polish capital in the aftermath of the Krakow attack.

The number of people wounded rose from 15 to 16, officials said late on Saturday. Authorities earlier said the gunman was 24 years old, but later corrected his age to 25.

———

Ciobanu reported from Warsaw, Poland and Dazio reported from Berlin.

This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/EU--Poland-Shooting-160651039.html

item.title: 伯克希尔加大股票回购力度
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

美国投资集团伯克希尔·哈撒韦11月7日公布第三季度财报，宣布当季斥资96亿美元回购公司股票，明显加快回购步伐，但保险业务疲软导致经营利润下降。

据路透社报道，伯克希尔第三季度经营利润为127.1亿美元，同比下降6%；净利润为221.1亿美元，同比下降28%，其中包含股票投资尚未实现的损益。

保险业务是利润下降的主要原因。保险承保利润同比下滑43%，旗下汽车保险公司Geico的税前利润下降45%，主要受到事故赔付增加及广告成本上升影响。

伯克希尔今年前两个季度已回购48亿美元股票，10月前四周又回购约20亿美元。公司9月底持有现金及短期投资约3569亿美元，仍拥有庞大的资金储备。

自格雷格·阿贝尔接任首席执行官以来，伯克希尔明显加快资金运用步伐。巴菲特目前担任公司荣誉董事长。

item.title: 俄军大规模空袭基辅军事及能源设施
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

俄罗斯11月7日表示，俄军夜间对乌克兰首都基辅及周边地区发动大规模导弹和无人机袭击，打击军事工业、能源和交通基础设施，造成多处设施受损。

俄罗斯国防部称，袭击击中基辅横跨第聂伯河的北方大桥，以及据称生产“火烈鸟”巡航导弹的Meridian工厂。俄方表示，该桥被乌军用于运输武器和军事车辆。

俄方还宣称，袭击摧毁或损坏基辅州的发电厂、变电站及弹药生产设施，并打击日托米尔州一座变电站，以及黑海上一艘据称运载军事及军民两用物资的货船。上述部分战果尚无法独立核实。

乌克兰官员证实，北方大桥及能源设施遭到袭击，基辅部分地区电力、供水和供暖受到影响。乌方称，俄军发射36枚弹道导弹及172架无人机，造成平民伤亡。

此次袭击发生在美俄乌准备于阿布扎比举行新一轮三方谈判之前。

俄乌战争

item.title: Trump officials weigh major overhaul of National Park and Fish and Wildlife services
item.description:
The Trump administration is considering a major reorganization of the National Park Service and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, according to internal documents reviewed by The Washington Post.

Staff are meeting this week and next to discuss a “realignment” of the two agencies, the documents show. One meeting regarding the National Park Service will discuss “pending duty station changes,” referring to the locations where staff report to work. But the documents do not specify whether certain offices would be closed or moved, or whether any employees would be fired.

The Interior Department, which oversees the agencies, did not respond to a request for comment.

Get Climate Coach newsletter

News and guidance on climate, science and technology. Sign up for free

Public land advocates fear that the changes could further hurt agencies that have already seen major staffing cuts since Trump began efforts to shrink the federal government by hundreds of thousands of employees last year.

“I think from their perspective, it seems as though that they’re trying to find efficiencies by consolidating staff within DOI that maybe served different functions across these agencies,” said Ed Stierli, vice president of government affairs at the National Parks Conservation Association, an advocacy group. “But I think in reality, it just seems to be causing more confusion and chaos.”

While the administration has considered differing plans to overhaul the Park Service since last year, including one reported in September by the Washington Sun, plans to reorganize the Fish and Wildlife Service are more recent. Fish and Wildlife manages more than 500 National Wildlife Refuges across the country, spanning 93 million acres.

A Fish and Wildlife Service report published on Friday recommends the agency “reduce headquarters and regional office staffing and reallocate positions to refuge operations, prioritizing the people needed to manage habitat, maintain facilities, support public access and protect resources.”

An internal communication to Fish and Wildlife Service staff on Friday, reviewed by The Post, states that the recommendations in the report “give us a path forward” and that “our next responsibility is to turn them into practical actions.”

In March, the administration initiated a reorganization of the U.S. Forest Service, which includes relocating its headquarters from Washington to Salt Lake City and hundreds of employees with it. The plan would also close some research stations and regional offices as it transitions to state offices.

A judge has put that plan on hold, as well as a wider reorganization of the Agriculture Department that oversees it, amid legal challenges.

Most Read From The Washington Post

  1. Stephen Miller’s promotion angers industries reeling from immigration enforcement
  2. Stephen Miller is named new White House chief of staff as Susie Wiles departs
  3. Hegseth draws fire after using government resources for partisan video
  4. Two more DOJ officials resign, including head of national security division
  5. Trump ally declines to back Hegseth when asked whether he should be replaced

At the Park Service, the administration has withheld millions in funding and cut Park Service staff by about a quarter, sometimes leading to long lines, fewer tours and dirty bathrooms at parks.

“When you talk about changing duty stations for example, are they just trying to cripple this agency?” Stierli asked. “Why would you try and sow chaos into an agency that is already stretched well beyond capacity trying to fulfill its mission?”

Bill Wade, executive director of the Association of National Park Rangers, which represents current and former Park Service employees, said that agency employees have had to live with the uncertainty and stress that major restructuring might be coming, possibly including layoffs, since the launch of the DOGE Service last year.

Based on the limited information about the current reorganization being considered, “it’s too little to try to determine what the impact would be on the service or employees,” Wade said.

It is unclear whether the current reorganization plans for the National Park Service had been significantly revised from earlier proposals. Layoff plans last year at the National Park Service, which have not been independently verified by The Post, were ultimately never carried out.

Stierli said that the administration appeared to “pump the brakes” on the plans two months ago, but it may now be feeling a new sense of urgency to restructure the agency with Democrats about to take control of Congress.

“Come January, you’re going have a new Congress who’s very eager to do oversight and pry into the National Park Service to look and see how staff are being organized, where is the budget for the Park Service going,” Stierli said.

In spending bills, congressional Democrats could write in provisions demanding approval over any restructuring in agencies, or at least to be notified, he said.

“We’re certainly hopeful that Congress uses this oversight power here, because I think what’s highly unusual is there’s been zero transparency,” Stierli added. “When there is zero transparency, it creates this confusion.”

This article originally appeared on Washington Post at https://www.washingtonpost.com/climate-environment/2026/11/07/trump-officials-consider-revamping-national-park-service-fish-wildlife-service/

item.title: 俄军导弹再袭基辅 乌总统和市长打嘴仗
item.link: https://www.dw.com/zh/俄军导弹再袭基辅 乌总统和市长打嘴仗/a-79885814
item.description:
德正
2026-11-07T14:56:52.388Z
11月7日凌晨，基辅消防人员正在试图扑灭俄军空袭引发的火灾

（德国之声中文网）乌克兰各地的气温正在持续下降，俄军也趁此再次对乌克兰的能源基础设施发动大规模打击。11月6日晚间、7日凌晨乌克兰首都基辅市中心及其周边地区多次传出爆炸声。

基辅市长克利奇科(Vitali Klitschko)在Telegram上表示，此次袭击使用了高超音速弹道导弹，防空系统极难将其拦截。袭击造成多栋住宅楼受损。军政管理当局还报告称，一间幼儿园在袭击中受损，另有两人受伤。

克利奇科表示，基辅目前的电力供应状况“极其困难”。此外，供水和集中供暖服务也受到了袭击的影响。一座横跨第聂伯河、连接基辅东西两岸的关键桥梁也遭到破坏。据克利奇科称，共有五人受伤。

总统和市长打嘴仗

在此之前，乌克兰总统泽连斯基曾录制视频，警告俄罗斯可能再次针对能源基础设施及横跨第聂伯河的桥梁发动袭击。在基辅等地大范围停电后，泽连斯基11月7日再次批评了克利奇科，称：“这是因为市政层面未能落实相关决策，导致未能做好准备应对供暖季、应对俄罗斯袭击能源设施。”

克利奇科则在Telegram上反唇相讥：“首都究竟该如何阻止这场‘俄罗斯针对乌克兰能源部门的特别行动’？”他指出，基辅自10月16日起就已经开始提供集中供暖。

除了基辅，乌克兰其他地区的电网也遭到了严重破坏。泽连斯基将此次针对能源基础设施的袭击描述为一场“混合型”攻击，其中包括36枚导弹和170多架无人机。

此外，在乌克兰南部村庄科米舒瓦哈(Komyschuwacha)，一处援助物资分发点遭到俄军空袭，导致55人丧生。

停火希望渺茫

乌克兰、俄罗斯和美国计划于下周在阿拉伯联合酋长国举行磋商——这是各方在相当长一段时间以来的首场此类谈判。据俄罗斯国际文传电讯社报道，俄方计划派遣一个由外交官和军方官员组成的高级别代表团，其中俄罗斯副外长里亚布科夫(Sergei Ryabkov)将首次加入谈判团队。

不过，德国国防部长皮斯托里乌斯(Boris Pistorius)认为，近期实现停火的希望十分渺茫。他在11月7日接受德国丰克媒体集团采访时表示，局势能否出现转机，取决于俄罗斯总统普京以及美国总统特朗普的行动。“过去几个月的情况表明，特朗普采取的方式很难迅速促成停火，更不用说实现和平了。”

乌克兰担心沦为美中俄三方峰会的筹码

就在两天前，美国总统特朗普刚刚声称，一项旨在结束俄乌战争的“极为重大”协议正在酝酿之中，该协议涉及俄罗斯。此前，特朗普在白宫与俄罗斯总统特使季米特里耶夫(Kirill Dmitriev)进行了一次计划外会晤。“这将是一项非常重大的协议。它所涉及的范围将不仅限于乌克兰——甚至可以说，它可能涉及整个欧洲。”特朗普还强调，结束这场战争可能需要“整个欧洲”的参与。

乌克兰总统泽连斯基则在接受美国CNN电视台采访时，就特朗普政府提议的所谓“新欧洲安全秩序构想”进行了警告。“坦白说，这绝非易事，甚至可能暗藏危险。……如果他们不谈论如何结束战争，那是非常危险的。俄罗斯却想直接从构建欧洲新安全架构谈起。”泽连斯基还强调，反对大国以牺牲欧盟、北约及其国家自身利益为代价达成任何协议。他表示：“我们都生活在欧洲。我们不希望再现‘雅尔塔’。”二战末期，苏联、美国、英国在克里米亚半岛的雅尔塔举行峰会，划分了在战后欧洲的势力范围。

美国总统特朗普、俄罗斯总统普京、中国国家主席习近平很有可能在11月中旬的深圳APEC峰会以及明年初的佛罗里达G20峰会上举行三方会晤。

item.title: 外帮人 你们错过了怎样的美味啊
item.description:
来源: 
桑陌

坐在院子里剥毛豆。讲是讲剥毛豆，其实不是用指甲剥的，是两只手扭的，一扭豆荚就开了。飘了一夜细雨，太阳一出来，满园湿润的草木清香。定定心心地剥毛豆，心无旁骛，轻松自在，几斤毛豆剥好，一点不恹气，甚至有点享受。

相似的场景小时候也有过，只是心境不同，那时剥毛豆是服苦役。娘娘以利相诱：剥好毛豆，给你调一碗可可豆溶粉。于是坐在天井的竹椅子上剥毛豆，地上一摊毛豆，剥好的毛豆放在淘箩里，豆壳丢在空篮子里。满心不耐烦，总觉得身上哪里发痒，手一搔，于是浑身发痒。好在会有小惊喜，豆荚剥开，里面有软软蠕动的小青虫。于是把小青虫归拢起来，连同那些被祸害的毛豆一起，放进纸盒里养。少时养的宠物都很袖珍，比如金龟虫，比如叫哥哥。小青虫不算的。等到想起它们，要么直直的一条干瘪了，要么蜷缩成一团出水了，那些咬过的豆还在。所以，小青虫不是死于食物的短缺，而是死于没了豆荚的庇护。那时没有绿色农产品的概念，现在有了，现在的毛豆里也看不到小青虫了。

当年，家里买毛豆，一买就是一大篮。娘娘先要过一遍，一节节捏过，把那些饱满的挑出来。剩下的剥毛豆，剥出来的毛豆子通常是炒咸菜，或者烧黄鱼鲞，也有在蒸苋菜梗或臭豆腐时抓一撮做点缀。那些挑选出来的饱满的毛豆，洗净沥干，两头剪掉少许尖角，以便入味，浸在苋菜梗的卤里。几天后捞出来，淋一点菜油，上锅蒸，蒸汽透出来，已经忍不住食指大动了。端上桌，异香扑鼻，入口，那种鲜臭霉香在嘴里爆开，直透五脏，每个毛孔都舒服得张开来，美不可言。绍兴话说的，下饭榔头，会多吃一碗饭。豆荚外面那层薄薄的绒毛也能吃，用牙齿篦下来吃，好吃。此菜名唤臭毛豆。有人把臭毛豆和豆豉搞混。豆豉是煮熟的黄豆发酵而成，也叫霉毛豆。臭毛豆是新鲜毛豆做的，在原汁原味的苋菜梗的卤里进行了一番浸润洗浴，出来摇身一变，成为绝品。苋菜梗的卤非常神奇，冬瓜、菜头、豆腐、毛豆都可以浸，浸好出来，各有风姿韵味。只是，一母所生也美丑妍媸不同，独领风骚的当数臭毛豆。天下美食，莫甚于此。由是，每年都会去几次绍兴，寻味苋菜梗大家族。

在绍兴老家，有把绍兴人以外的人统称为外帮人的习惯。外帮人一词并无贬义。有客来，端上桌的必有苋菜梗臭毛豆，这是绍兴人待上宾之谊。通常来客并不领情。于是主人笑着自我解嘲：噢，怠慢了，你是外帮人，吃不惯的。我常常庆幸自己不是外帮人，否则就无缘消受如此美味了。偶尔，我也会以同情且狭隘的心理看外帮人，他们错过了怎样的美味啊。

早些年，我搬一座盆景，屏了一屏，左眼视网膜脱落了。开好刀，在家休养，还不能朝天睡，必须合扑睡。老妻看我可怜，每天贴心地问我想吃什么。对病人来说，好像最大的安慰，就是打发他吃些好吃的食物。我报出来的都是家常菜，咸菜炒乌贼、桂花肉、肉饼子炖蛋、苋菜梗、臭毛豆之类。老妻的评价是，吃相好的，好服侍的，可惜苋菜梗和臭毛豆买不到。女儿回家，也是问我想吃什么。我脱口而出，可可豆溶粉。少时放学回家，娘娘会给我冲调一碗可可豆溶粉，掺杂着可可的醇香和黄豆的清香，还有糯米的黏香，解馋还垫饥。可惜再也吃不到娘娘调的可可豆溶粉了。我交代说，可可豆溶粉的包装，和装蚊香的圆筒差不多大小，外面涂了一层防潮的蜡。女儿不耐烦，说，不要翻老皇历好吧，上网搜了，搜不到。也是，即使买到了，大抵也不复当年的味道了。

吃相，是从娘胎里带来的，是自小在餐桌上形成的，是刻在骨子里的乡恋。没有吃过的食物，你不会馋。让你心心念念惦记的，大抵是往日留在味蕾上的记忆，一旦记忆浮现，那便是馋虫爬出来的时候。

关键词: 
毛豆
绍兴
美食
栏目: 
品味生活
栏目重点发表: 
栏目头条
作者: 
桑陌

item.title: 在诊室里用豆包的医生们
item.description:
来源: 
显微故事

10月25日，江苏徐州某医院的心血管科诊室，一个医生在听患者病情时打开了豆包。最后患者拒绝了医生开的处方。

事情发酵之后，医生所在的医院做了核实，给出了一条被患者家属镜头漏掉的信息：医生查的是一个新药，发现不适合这位患者，当天并没有开出任何新处方。

医院方强调，“AI只是用来获取信息的辅助，处方权始终在医生手里。”

随着AI的告诉发展，如今不仅许多患者在就医前习惯查询一下豆包，许多医生也确实在日常工作中会使用AI进行信息的补充搜索。

据行业访谈与媒体引用，豆包日均健康类咨询量被估在2000万人次量级（字节未正式披露精确数），相当于把过去“百度健康搜索”的流量迁到了对话框里

根据丁香园发布了一份针对647名医务工作者的调研，其中有98.5%的医生在过去三个月工作中用过AI，70.8%的医生每周至少使用数次，81.4%的医生用过豆包。

在诊室停滞的那几秒钟里，原本只属于医生和患者之间的沟通，被一个看不见摸不着的第三方插入了，传统的医患关系被悄然改变。

作者访问到了在诊室里使用AI的医生：

问了问他们到底如何看待AI，平时在哪些情况下会使用AI辅助，更值得我们关心的是，这些医生究竟用在哪一步，又在哪条线上自己刹住了？

以下是关于他们的真实故事：

1

药典在住院部， 豆包在手机里

去年开始，洪医生就尝试过在面诊时用豆包了。

在洪医生的患者里，有一位52岁的中老年女性，对方有8年类风湿关节炎病史，长期在口服甲氨蝶呤片治疗，临床症状控制得不错。

那次挂号，是因为患者表示自己近几日尿频尿急，在一系列门诊检查后，结果显示有细菌感染，洪医生考虑是单纯性尿路感染。

洪医生说，当时他首先判断是想开具对症的复方磺胺甲噁唑，“这是该病的一线用药之一，而且便宜、有效。”洪医生告诉记者。

处方写到一半，洪医生忽然想起，这位患者之前有用过甲氨蝶呤片的情况，印象中这两种药一起使用似乎是有一定排斥反应。

甲氨蝶呤的使用说明书

“甲氨蝶呤主要经肾小管分泌排泄，复方磺胺甲噁唑里的甲氧苄啶也走这条路，理论上会竞争排泄，抬高甲氨蝶呤血药浓度。但临床上的风险到底有多大？是尽量避免，还是密切监测血象就可以用？”

以往这种情况，洪医生会去翻看药典确认。但那天药典正好放在住院部的办公室里，不在手边，于是洪医生下意识掏出手机，在豆包里输入“甲氨蝶呤 复方磺胺甲噁唑 相互作用 骨髓抑制”。

豆包很快给出了几行提示。其中一条非常明确：

复方磺胺甲噁唑可显著增加甲氨蝶呤的血药浓度，两者联用骨髓抑制风险升高，严重时可致全血细胞减少，建议避免联用；

另一条提示是若必须联用，需密切监测血常规和甲氨蝶呤血药浓度，并考虑减量。

还有一条她记到现在：这种相互作用在低剂量方案里同样存在，不只是大剂量化疗才要警惕。

于是，洪医生删掉了复方磺胺甲噁唑，换了另一种抗生素。“我没有拿它开药下诊断，这个工具更像一个随身药典。”

2

医生你看，豆包确实是这么说的

和洪医生不同，呼吸科的罗医生最近最苦恼的，反而是病人反复拿自己在豆包上搜过的结果来“拷问”自己。

在诊室里先掏出手机查询AI的，可能不是医生，也可能是患者。

令他印象最深刻的，是今年一位50多岁的中年男性患者。

该患者在公司组织体检时，发现了右肺有一个约6mm的纯磨玻璃结节。

洪医生看了对方的CT检查报告，其中显示结节边界清楚，密度均匀，没有实性成分。

以洪医生的诊断，按肺结节诊治共识，这种程度的肺结节，首选定期随访，定期复查CT。

但是患者先把手机递了过来。屏幕上是豆包的对话：“磨玻璃结节可能是早期肺腺癌，建议尽早手术切除。”

“罗医生你看嘛，我查了，豆包说可能是癌，我想直接切掉。”

要是在早几年前，罗医生肯定会跟病人说“网上说啥你们就信啥？”。

但现在不一样了，罗医生心里也很清楚，AI盛行的科技时代，这些患者接触医学不可能只通过医生和医院，他们会检索会思考，会有更多的意见可参考。

但问题在于，患者没有医学背景，他们在搜索过程中大多描述症状，却不能准确地将医学相关的提示词指出，描述的方法不同会导致AI出现的结果截然相反。

罗医生把患者的胸部CT调了出来，找到结节位置，开始和患者详细解释了目前的情况，最后还指导患者把问豆包的问题改得更贴合他自己的病情一些。

患者改了一下，屏幕上的回答变了，给出的结论和罗医生的建议大致相同。

“AI不是错了，有时候它会看人下菜碟。同一个问题，我们医生问，它给的是针对性的指南；换一个没有医学背景的患者来问，可能就是大范围的笼统答案。”罗医生和记者解释。

但这种做法还是没有让患者放心，因为他认识的一个邻居也是肺结节，手术做出来就是癌。

为了进一步降低患者的焦虑，罗医生不得不把他所知的信息再掰开了、揉碎了讲给患者：

目前恶性概率不高，随访是更合理的选择；现在手术，切掉的是一辈子的肺功能，换来的可能是一个“本来就不需要切”的结节。

哪怕是这样的耐心，患者也没有被当场说服，继而又追问罗医生，“随访过程中结节要是还在变大怎么办？”

那天门诊，罗医生在这个患者身上花了将近半小时。

“如果每个病人都拿着豆包搜过的内容进来和我讨论，那整体的医疗效率会变得越来越慢”，罗医生表示。

或许如果没有AI那一段，这个患者十分钟内就能沟通完。但患者带着一个“可能是癌”的答案进来，就必须先把这个答案拆开，再把医生的判断装回去。

同一间诊室，同一个工具，在医生手里和在患者手里，触发的是完全不同的信任反应。

医生把AI当做药典，而患者却把AI直接当成了医生。

3

病例里的“漂亮话”

发生在豆包、元宝、千问等AI工具里的医疗咨询，已经是AI时代下的大势所趋。

本质上，用它们查病，和用百度搜病，都是一类的人。但不同的是，搜索引擎能给出的答案有限，AI通常会更细致地询问你的病情，给出更多“看起来很专业”的建议。

前段时间网络上还曾出现过一张热图：在医院的门诊室门口贴着一张字条，上面写着“已经在豆包获得诊断的患者，请勿再向我们寻求建议。”

虽然这张图已经被认定为人为生成，不是真实图片，但还是反映出了当下一部分地区医患关系中对豆包AI这类工具的态度——“如果有豆包，还要医生干嘛？”

但事实是，在我们所访问的几个三甲医院的医生都表示，AI不是洪水猛兽，在医疗中使用AI早已经是大势所趋，关键点不在于用不用，而是怎么用？何时用？用在哪些方面。

西南地区某二甲医院呼吸内科的主任陈医生和记者表示，这几个月医院开了几次会议，征求中层干部意见，主要讨论要不要在医生工作系统中引入AI。

在陈医生眼里，AI对医疗的好处是很明确的。

语音转文字、结构化初稿、缺项提醒，能显著压缩文书时间，病历规范性也更稳定。

“病历系统的AI确实在变强”，陈医生说到，有的医院上线大模型病历系统后，书写效率提升数倍，甲级病历率提高到97%以上。

此外，之前也有媒体报道过，武汉一家医院投用AI语音病历后，医生日均节省近三小时，病历合格率提升到99%。

“从质控指标上看，AI的答卷相当好看，”陈医生说。但陈医生还是在会议上投了拒绝引入AI一票。

“AI的弊端也显而易见”，陈医生说。

陈医生给科里的年轻医生讲过自己当住院医时手写病历的经历。在他那里，每天查房，患者的病情变化必须由主管医生亲自记录——哪怕那条记录最后只有一行。

“AI不会替你查房，也不会替你观察病人的病情变化。AI写的是一份完美病历应该有的样子，不是这个病人实际的样子。”

病人回答病史会有隐瞒，AI可能遗漏关键信息；更深一层，年轻医生可能跳过“自己归纳、鉴别、判断”的训练，只学会点“确认”。

因此，陈医生最关心的不是病历写得有多好看，他最担心的是，在没有限定好规则和使用方法时，盲目引入AI会带来的隐患。

“甲级病历率是次要的，真正关系到病人安全的是，这份病历里到底有多少是医生真正观察到的，又有多少是AI按模板和上下文自己‘补’出来的。”

比如，如果病人只在床边说了一句“昨晚烧到39度”，那么AI能很快顺着上下文补全病人的起病缓急、热型、伴随症状，个个有模有样。

“这些句子可能无中生有、与事实不符，或者漏掉关键细节”，陈医生说，可怕的是，目前它们未必会被我们现阶段的AI质控抓住。

“我们的质检系统也在用AI，但现阶段在病历的质检上，AI查得是病历结构是否完整，逻辑是否自洽”，陈医生说，“至于这句话到底是不是病人的诊室情况，AI判断不出来”。

“一份病历写得再规范，如果里头有一句假话，它就是一份假病历。质控分数不会告诉你这件事，病人出事的时候，律师会告诉你。”

今年1月，张文宏在香港高山书院十周年论坛也表过态，拒绝把AI引入医生的日常生活，“你可以自己在那里用，但是不允许在我的病历系统里面用AI”。

张文宏的理由是，如果实习医生直接通过AI得出结论，没经过系统的训练，最后就很难自己鉴别AI是对还是错。

监管的线其实已经画了：2022年2月试行的《互联网诊疗监管细则》写得明白，处方必须由接诊医师本人开具，禁止使用人工智能等自动生成处方，此后北京、上海、福建等地陆续跟进，口径一致。

落到病历上，是同一个道理——AI可以写，但认账的必须是签字的人。

3

健康和效率，不该出现在天平的两端

还是回到那个问题，医生和患者到底该不该用AI。答案是肯定，但使用的方法需要注意。

在我们走访的几家医院，医生都表示从个人角度，AI的使用并不是洪水猛兽，豆包、元宝、千问等AI工具的存在其实是有利于医生去查询资料的，关键看医生自己要利用专业能力去有效判断。

洪医生把AI的边界划分得很清楚。

仅拿查药品这件事情来说，一个医生在临床工作中遇到拿不准的细节，停下来“翻书”这件事本身不新鲜。

未出现AI时，上一代医生翻药典、查文献、打电话问上级，这一代医生从纸张和搜索引擎，变成了一个豆包、千问、元宝等AI工具里，会组织语言、会给出“建议”的对话框。

洪医生如今依然会使用AI，但她主要用来查询不常规用药的说明书，核查一些药物之间的相互作用。有时，遇到多病共存、多重用药的患者时，她会使用AI看看有没有漏掉的坑。

但她从来不会问“这个病人该用什么药”，也从不把AI的输出直接写进处方。

对她来说，豆包这类AI工具，“就像一个反应很快的临床药师，知识面广”，洪医生告诉记者，“你可以问它，但不能让它签字，也不能让它担责。”

罗医生也找到了和用豆包来看病的患者之间的相处方式。

“如果患者进门先说‘我查了豆包’”，他不急着否定，也不顺着走。“我会看患者查询时如何描述的，再看AI给了几种可能，最后会问患者自己觉得哪一种最符合。”

三个步骤下来，通常就能把对话从“AI说的”拉回到“患者身上到底发生了什么”。如果遇到AI列出的可能性里确实有一条值得排查，就会当场解释原因。

“现在医生、患者和AI之间感觉是一个三角关系，而想要这个关系达到稳定，是需要医生的解释。医生解释得不够详细，患者就会自己去找答案。而他们找到的方向，未必通向正确。归根到底还是需要打铁自身硬。”

陈医生也不反对AI，甚至如今他自己也用，“遇到拿不准的鉴别方向、记不清的药物相互作用，会打开对话框查一下。”

但他依然坚信，写病历从来不是文书工作，是临床思维的训练场。

年轻医生在反复推敲主诉怎么归纳、现病史留哪些细节、鉴别诊断按什么顺序排的过程中，才有可能慢慢长出一条属于自己的路。

（应受访者要求，本文出现人物除公开人物以外均为化名，文中出现的药品和诊断结果仅为稿件撰写需要，不能作为任何辅助诊断信息。）

关键词: 
AI
看病
豆包
栏目: 
品味生活
首页重点发表: 
Flash

item.title: 攻破币安的 不过是一份简历
item.description:
来源: 
荐叔

讲个故事。史上最大加密货币盗窃案的最新进展来了。币安刚刚公布了 63 亿美元被盗的完整调查报告。这份报告非常详细，把自己是怎么被攻破的，一步一步写了出来。整个过程让人后背发凉，比好莱坞电影还要惊心动魄。另一方面，美国 FBI 指控，这是朝鲜的黑客组织 UNC4899 干的，这个组织隶属于大名鼎鼎的” 拉撒路 “，这个组织的黑客纪录包括 12 年前黑进索尼影业，还有累计金额超 10 亿美元的全球银行攻击。当然这只是美方的单方说法，朝鲜方面坚决否认，称这是” 荒唐无稽的谣言”。

最让人目瞪口呆的是，这次 63 亿美元惊天盗案的起点竟然是四个月前，一个币安工程师在求职平台上收到的一条私信。

事情的来龙去脉是这样的。今年 6 月份，币安钱包开发团队的一名工程师，想装一款热门的 AI 编程工具，就在网上搜了一个安装包。他不知道的是，这个安装包是假的。黑客把恶意版本放进了搜索引擎广告，让它的排名比正版还靠前。” 特洛伊木马 “就这么装进了他的电脑。但币安的安全团队很快发现了异常，删掉了软件，还给这个工程师更换了设备，重置了所有凭证。看起来危机已经解除。但谁也没想到，黑客真正想要的东西，已经拿到手了：这名工程师的岗位、职责，以及他所在的钱包团队里还有哪些人，分别管什么。

三个月后，一个有跳槽意向的币安工程师在一个正规求职平台上收到一条私信，对方自称是某家公司的项目总监。这家公司是虚构的。第一轮面试是视频，面试官还主动打开自己的社交账号，没有任何异常。第二轮面试，换到一个社交聊天软件上，对方称自己是这家公司的 CEO，然后发来一份面试作业，让他下载下来做。问题就在这份面试作业上。这是个代码库，里面藏着一段专门定制的木马。工程师的电脑就这么被黑客操控了，一切神不知鬼不觉。

币安在报告里写，这段恶意软件用了非常复杂的伪装和规避技术，把一个正常组件替换成了恶意版本，然后向币安服务器发指令。币安所有的终端安全工具，都没有发现并报警。一个面试求职的币安工程师，就这么自家公司的门，打开了一条缝。

搞定这一切后，黑客并没有急着动手。他们用控制的这台电脑，加上币安内部的一款 AI 工具，去控制另外两名币安钱包工程师的电脑。其中一个人，正是 6 月份中招的那位。他手上有一个关键权限：可以把代码发布到生产系统。攻击者要的就是这个。

直到 10 月 29 日深夜，攻击者远程登录第三名工程师的电脑，运行了一段恶意脚本。他们利用以太坊的一个技术标准，拿到了币安一个热钱包的链上执行授权。这个授权，没有走币安正常的审批流程。从那一刻开始，20 分钟，63.4 亿美元，从 5 个热钱包里被转走，跨了 10 条区块链。转完之后，他们启动了自毁机制，把所有用过的工具和痕迹全部删掉。一起惊天盗案至此已成。

听到这里，你还觉得这起史上最大虚拟币盗案和你无关吗？攻破币安的，不是多么高深的密码学，不过是一份简历。在这个 AI 时代，你投出去的简历，你收到的邮件，你下载的文件，都可能是递给别人的一把钥匙。

关键词: 
币安
黑客
木马
栏目: 
品味生活
作者: 
荐叔

item.title: 五中全会后北京高层各怀心事
item.description:
来源: 
上报

中共当局提前在二十届五中全会宣布，涉及高层换届的二十一大将于2027年下半年举行。而按惯例这是在六中全会才宣布的。这一变化意味着中南海的政治部署整体往前移了。

这种变化的背后是什么？

习近平因“放心不下”做出妥协

种种官方信息已表明，1953年生的习近平，寻求二十一大连任已不言而喻。当局提前宣布二十一大时间，等于权力布局提速，背后是习近平担心连任出现突发干扰，要及早筹备。这也是他所谓“时时放心不下”的真实意涵。

五中全会的主题是全面从严治党，实际上就是搞政治斗争。但会后出炉的“全面从严治党”决定，却意外对党内民主部分着墨十分详细。比如强调要严格贯彻执行民主集中制，各级“一把手”不得搞“一言堂”“家长制”，也不得层层要求维护“一把手”个人权威。

有人说，这是中央全会对习近平推行“集权”、搞一人统治有所“隐晦批评”。但笔者认为，更准确说，是习对党内有所妥协。

文革之后，邓小平掌权时期制定了《关于党内政治生活的若干准则》（1980年），主要针对毛泽东独裁专权，强调“坚持集体领导，反对个人专断”，强调民主集中制及“发扬党内民主”。

但习近平本来对“党内民主”十分忌讳。2021年6月29日官方公开他2018年1月在中纪委全会上的讲话，他当时批评，那些“强调党的集中统一已经够充分了，今后要把重心放在发展党内民主上”的说法是“奇谈怪论”。

近年中共高层会议通稿均强调“集中统一领导”，很少再提“民主集中制”。2024年底前，中共军报曾连续发文强调“集体领导”和“党内民主”的重要性，或是不满习近平的军委副主席张又侠一派发出的声音。

所以这次五中全会文件大谈党内民主，就比较罕见，可以视为习近平认怂退让，以换取中央委员支持他二十一大连任。

需要注意的是，习近平在五中全会做了一个保权的动作，就是拍板增选军委副主席张升民进入政治局。他要拉拢枪杆子，对党内示威，警告大家别蠢蠢欲动。

但张升民也有自己的算计，也就是现在军中人事，其实就是他说了算，习近平是两眼一抹黑，还得靠张升民帮助把关，结果上来的就是“张家军”。

张升民1958年生，目前看来他留任的机会还比较大。因为中共五中全会最新强调了“选拔干部不唯年龄学历”，这就是为那些延期任职的老迈高官准备了后门。

李强谋连任恐遭暗算

中共总理李强1959年出生，目前外界多认为他会在二十一大留任。

港媒《明报》报导，李强在中共二十大当上常委后，就派人日夜守卫浙江温州老家的祖坟。这在中国传统中是保官运之举，说明李强希望祖先保佑日后继续上位。

李强当总理以来，看似弱势，但他未必没有野心。在我看来，他只是俗语所说的“扮猪吃老虎”，暂时隐忍。因为习没有安排接班人，假若习突然死去，按理李强是第一顺位顶上。

不过，李强有一个大的软肋：2023年9月他刚上任几个月，妻子、女儿的详细信息及敛财黑料就在网络上被曝光。

当时一个名为“中国前线”的Blogger博客爆料称，李强的夫人林环为浙江商业研究所所长，利用丈夫的权力搞政商关系，光在马云创办的蚂蚁金服就拥有股权逾500亿人民币，其家族总资产在800亿到1000亿之间。

爆料还称，李强女儿李颖是习近平的乾女儿，入读上海同济大学，毕业后在一家刚成立、注册资金只有30万美元的世函盛建筑设计公司（SHL）混得风生水起。世函盛全靠李强才能拿到标案。李强的洋女婿名叫Hardie Christopher Forbes。

这些爆料曾引发轰动，到了2023年10月2日左右，爆料博客突然被删除。

这次中共五中全会出炉的“全面从严治党决定”，要求加强对领导干部及其家属的监督，重点查处领导干部家族式腐败。虽然这种套路很旧，但放到现在，会成为中共高层新一轮相互攻击的重要内容。

李强谋求连任，很可能被政敌在二十一大前的关键时间拿这些材料进行攻击。

赵乐际盼退休不被翻旧帐

1957年生的赵乐际，担任两届常委后，到二十一大铁定要退休了。但他希望获得习的安全保证，以免他在倒查风中被翻旧帐。

赵乐际涉及两大案。

其一是秦岭违建别墅案。2018年7月，习近平第六次批示整治秦岭违建别墅未果，愤而掀翻一大批对他阳奉阴违的官员，包括陕西前省委书记赵正永等人。但其实大部分别墅是在赵乐际2007至2012年执掌陕西期间修建的。《明报》曾披露，赵乐际因为陕西秦岭违建别墅案，曾受到习近平的警告。

另外，陕西商人赵发琦在陕西北部榆林横山县榆横矿区等价值千亿的矿权被夺的案件，涉及最高法院院长周强及时任陕西省委书记赵乐际下指示干扰司法。此事2018年底经前央视主持人崔永元和最高法院主审该案的法官王林清联手曝光，之后他们均受到打压，其中王林清入狱。

背负两大案的赵乐际能在二十大留任常委，应该是他和习近平达成了妥协的结果，习近平当时需要联合赵乐际等人，集中清理团派势力。但到二十一大赵乐际彻底退休后，他会不会被揪出，或以某种方式打击，就很难说了。

王沪宁欲退而不休？

1955年生的王沪宁已任两届常委，中共二十一大不可能留在常委位置，他可能寻求转任国家副主席。即便退休，也要搞个退而不休的特别模式。

王沪宁被称为“三朝国师”，曾为江泽民、胡锦涛分别炮制了“三个代表”、“科学发展观”，“习近平思想”也出自他的手。习近平的“一带一路”、“人类命运共同体”，再到统战台湾的两岸融合发展示范区，都出自王沪宁的谋划。

中共二十一大习近平要再连任，缺乏合法性，恐怕站不住脚，所以他还是需要王沪宁勉为其难，在退休之后也指导一帮御用文人炮制点理论，毕竟朝中无人了。

王沪宁至今仍挂着中央深改委办主任的职务，中央深改委负责最高顶层设计。而中央政策研究室与中央深改委办仍是合署办公，二十大后虽然王沪宁已转任政协主席，中央政策研究室也换了主任，但实际上这个智囊班子还是王沪宁在管。

王沪宁从政治局退出之后，如果不能当国家副主席，很可能挂一个顾问式的职务，暗控中央深改委办和中央政策研究室。当然，他的这种谋划，背后有彭丽媛的支持。

王沪宁的现任（第三任）妻子是青岛人，1985年出生，比王沪宁小30岁，传闻原是中央警卫局服务处的保健员，与王沪宁2014年5月结婚，当时是彭丽媛帮忙牵了红线，也有说法指该女子就是彭丽媛的亲戚。

如果王沪宁退而不休，也让人有另一种想象，在习近平不能视事之时，王沪宁可能以“国师”的声望，支持彭丽媛“接班”。

蔡奇的儿子是其软肋

1955年生的蔡奇，也可能争取连任常委。五中全会“决定”列明“选拔干部不唯年龄学历”，应该也是蔡奇大力支持的。

蔡奇现在是习近平身边的头号红人。他以中共中央政治局常委的身分兼任中央办公厅主任，又是中央党建领导小组组长、国家安全委员会副主席、中央党校校长、中央和国家机关工委书记，权力涉及安全、宣传、党务、机要、人事以及网络监控等多个要害部门。

由于负责习近平的安保和保健、生活起居，蔡奇成了最接近习的高官，他很可能以习的安全保障为由，争取留任常委。当然蔡奇留任也是习近平的政治需要，习实在找不到这样忠于他的人了。

蔡奇如果不能连任，他最希望能转任国家副主席。这和王沪宁的计划有些冲突。

蔡奇也有软肋，他的软肋不在落马的旧部问题上，比如北京前政协主席魏小东、北京前常务副市长夏林茂，蔡奇可以说他们的靠山另有其人，推给陈希，推得乾乾净净。因为所有中管干部，名单都是时任中组部部长陈希向习近平推荐上去的。

蔡奇的软肋在儿子身上。蔡奇之子蔡尔津现任国家发改委低空经济发展司副司长。

低空经济本来是新兴的油水领域。但自从今年6月北京最高楼“中国尊”撞机事件发生后，无人机受严控，低空经济产业政策收紧，浙江、广东等多地先后宣布，拟废止或暂停低空经济产业的财政补贴文件，或调整奖补政策。在习近平政治安全第一之下，这个产业接下来发展难度加大，甚至可能被扼杀。

蔡尔津早前已经卷入一些企业利益输送的丑闻。五中全会出炉文件要查领导干部家族式腐败，日后肯定就会有人举报蔡尔津，举报的人多了，或者举报的人级别高了，对蔡奇在二十一大的仕途走向就有影响。

丁薛祥想学华国锋走捷径

1962年生的丁薛祥，是最年轻的二十届政治局常委，他留任常委是最正常的。

习近平的身体状况近年已大不如前。笔者此前就讲过，丁薛祥很有心机，一直盼习“驾崩”前，能留下遗言让他接班，就像当年毛泽东临终前指定华国锋接班一样。

毛泽东在世时，曾赞华国锋是“老实人”，“办事不蠢”。在大跃进及随后的政治斗争中，华国锋坚决维护毛泽东，“绝不怀疑，绝不动摇，绝不含糊”。在毛泽东病重之际，给华国锋写下“你办事，我放心”。这成为后来华国锋接掌最高权力的政治依据。

丁薛祥颇像华国锋，他学识和能力有限，但长期当秘书，善于揣摩习的意图，甚得习的欢心，所以获一路提拔。在中共二十大上他被塞进常委会，次年当上常务副总理。

2019年，丁薛祥曾露骨解读“两个维护”（意思是维护习近平的核心地位和权威）的对象，只是习近平而不是其他任何人。他还说，“两个维护”既不能层层套用，也不能随意延伸。2022年二十大后，丁薛祥在党媒放话“在斗争中巩固和增强团结”，呼应习近平所提的“风高浪急甚至惊涛骇浪”。丁薛祥这些表态都令习感到“放心”。

丁薛祥虽然在家族腐败问题上尚没有把柄落在人手，但他之前拉上来的江苏“南通帮”小弟、国家外汇管理局局长朱鹤新，不知被谁举报了，导致五中全会递补中央委员时被跳过。这对丁薛祥也算是不利消息。

李希与两人争当国家副主席

1956年生的李希，掌管中纪委后，“打虎”力度大于前两任——王岐山和赵乐际。但因为得罪太多人，面临在二十一大退休，他也有点担心被清算。

李希是甘肃两当人，他曾大力推动把自己老家这个习仲勋起家之地开发成为红色景点。在担任延安市委书记期间，李希又将习近平早年当知青的梁家河，打造成为现今官员趋之若鹜的朝拜地。故深得习的信任。

李希现在盘算的也是与习近平讨价还价，以获得保证：退休后不被翻旧帐。李希在任广东省委书记时，时任省长是马兴瑞。早有爆料指李希卷入马兴瑞案，把柄在查办马兴瑞的中纪委副书记刘金国手上。

李希想尽量不退休，而是转任有“第八常委”之称的国家副主席。这就涉及到他和王沪宁、蔡奇的竞争了。

国家副主席，过去基本上是由政治局常委担任的权威实职，胡锦涛、曾庆红和习近平都担任过，但到习上台后，李源潮仅以政治局委员身分担任此职，变成纯粹礼仪角色。后来两任国家副主席，王岐山和韩正，均只是前政治局常委。

王岐山从中纪委书记变成国家副主席之后，曾公开对“充当礼仪角色”感到愤愤不平。他可能没料到，现在这份闲职成了多名临退的常委争夺的目标。

政局纷乱“人算不如天算”

近期不少人在分析或猜测中共二十一大的入局、入常名单。

但入常、入政治局的名单，恐怕一直要斗到二十一大的最后一刻才定局。比如有望入常的胡春华，在二十大闭幕会前临时被换名单，前总书记胡锦涛正因为要看这份名单而被习近平找人强架出会场。

高层换届人事，还会有一些异数。比如中共历史上有中央委员“跳级”，不经政治局委员阶段，直接入常：如1992年十四大上的胡锦涛、2007年十七大上的习近平和李克强，胡锦涛当时为西藏自治区党委书记、习近平为上海市委书记、李克强为辽宁省委书记，他们当时都只是中央委员。这种情况往往与领导人的接班安排有关，如果出现，是一个敏感的信号。

说实在话，古今中外，政治的事，有时一天都嫌长，中国人更讲“人算不如天算”。虽然中共当局早早就宣布2027年下半年要开二十一大，但在这个时间点之前，政局会不会因某些事件而发生突变？若中共突然遭解散，党代会就开不成了。这也是许多人不敢想象的！

关键词: 
中共
栏目: 
新颖视角
作者: 
杜政

item.title: Wisconsin trooper released from ICE custody after 'dramatic experience'
item.description:
A 21-year-old South African-born Wisconsin State Patrol trooper who was detained Nov. 5 by federal immigration agents was released from custody Nov. 6, according to his attorney.

Attorney Marc Christopher confirmed to the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe, who was traveling to visit family with a valid work permit, had been released from the Dodge County Jail and was awaiting a ride from his supervisor, the head trooper in Tomah.

Christopher said Van Der Merwe was released under an order of supervision, which requires him to periodically check in with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. He will also likely be subject to electronic monitoring, potentially through an application on his cellphone rather than an ankle bracelet.

Christopher said he plans to speak with Van Der Merwe to discuss the next steps in his case. He expects Van Der Merwe will eventually share his experience publicly but wants to give him time to readjust following his release.

"I just told him I wanted him to get back, get reacclimated, just get settled, because I know he's gone through a very dramatic experience," Christopher said.

Van Der Merwe came to the U.S. from South Africa with his family on visas at age 14, Christopher said. His family has been waiting seven years for their asylum case to be heard.

Earlier, Christopher slammed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement for detaining a Wisconsin law enforcement officer who has permission to work, saying he was "flabbergasted" by the agents' decision to use its resources to target Van Der Merwe.

"I almost can't even believe that they would be so brazen as to do this. But they are," Christopher said. "There's no reason for them to detain him other than to indiscriminately pick up as many people as they can."

Van Der Merwe, who lived in New Mexico with his family, wanted to serve in the U.S. military, but could not because he was not a permanent resident, Christopher said. He graduated with a degree in criminal justice in New Mexico, then researched states where he could do similar work with his status and found Wisconsin.

Van Der Merwe was living in Onalaska and working in Tomah for the Wisconsin State Patrol over the past year. His work authorization is valid until 2030.

Attorney disputes ICE's assertion about legal status

ICE's argument is that Van Der Merwe – as a teenager in the U.S. with his family – overstayed his visitor's visa.

"He entered the country in March 2019 with legal permission to stay until September 2019. In defiance of our nation’s laws, he overstayed his admission," a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said in a statement. "Work authorization or a pending application do not confer legal status in the U.S."

Christopher pushed back on that assertion.

"That is just absurd and ridiculous," Christopher said. "They've been here lawfully. They have been waiting for their application to be adjudicated and to be decided by immigration."

The family, who are White South Africans, had applied for asylum on the grounds they were persecuted. A family member had been attacked, Christopher said.

Van Der Merwe did not decide to come to the U.S. himself, as he was brought by his parents, and he chose a career in law enforcement to serve his new country, Christopher said.

ICE agents detained him Nov. 5 at the Dane County Regional Airport just after he went through security, Christopher said. He was traveling to visit his family in New Mexico. Agents handcuffed him, shackled his legs and put him in a van and drove him to Dodge County Jail, which holds ICE detainees.

Christopher said it seems that the Transportation Security Administration tipped off ICE when he bought his ticket, and agents met Van Der Merwe at the airport. Christopher has heard of ICE making arrests at the Milwaukee and Appleton airports through similar tip-offs, he said.

Lawyer hopes Congress changes the way ICE can operate

Under the Trump administration, ICE has not been setting bond for detainees voluntarily unless a judge orders it. Trump administration policy changes have made many detainees ineligible to even seek bond and leave detention.

Christopher said he hopes Wisconsin's congressional delegation takes note of the case and institutes changes to the way ICE can operate. He was critical that ICE would use its resources to arrest Van Der Merwe, then hold him in custody.

"You're going to use your resources to go after this guy? You're going to use our tax dollars to detain this guy? It doesn't make any sense," Christopher said.

As part of its summer surge in street arrests in Milwaukee, ICE arrested a 20-year-old Milwaukee man, Giovanni Sosa, who had lived in the U.S. since age 4. In detaining him, ICE gave him paperwork that said – at age 4 – he had overstayed his visa. Sosa spent a month in detention at the Dodge County Jail as he waited for the chance to post bond.

Sophie Carson is a general assignment reporter who reports on religion and faith, immigrants and refugees and more. Contact her at scarson@gannett.com or 920-323-5758.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Wisconsin trooper released from ICE custody after 'dramatic experience'

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY at https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2026/11/07/wisconsin-trooper-released-from-ice-custody/92660641007/

item.title: FAA 计划到 2028 年淘汰软盘
item.description: FAA 计划到到 2028 年底前更换全美逾 400 个空管设施使用的软盘。新系统 Enterprise Information Display System 将取代可上溯至 1980 年代的旧系统。逾 25 年前软盘就基本停止使用，2011 年起不再大规模生产。去年美国国会批准了 125 亿美元资金用于更新陈旧的空管系统。FAA 目前还面临诸多技术难题，交通部长 Sean Duffy 正寻求额外 30 亿美元的资金。FAA 局长 Bryan Bedford 表示：“我们正摒弃过时的手动流程，用一套现代化系统取代曾依赖软盘的技术。新系统使管制员能即时共享关键的飞行警报、空域限制计划以及飞行员报告。”FAA 还在使用康柏（Compaq）计算机，此类计算机所需的零部件更换是靠 eBay 购买的。

item.title: 魔都行客｜上海英语新教材，“Alice /Cindy”变成“xinxin/shenshen”，怎么读？
item.description: 英语新教材发下来，一堆用拼音来读的人名：xinxin、shenshen、xiao pu, xiao jiang……“shenshen”=申申，“xiao pu”=小浦，“xiao jiang”=小江。如果角色定位是中国人，那会话就讲中文好了。

item.title: ESA Hera 探测器发回 DART 撞击的小行星照片
item.description: ESA Hera 探测器拍下了 Didymos 双小行星系统的首张近距离照片。这个系统由两颗小行星组成，直径 780 米的 Didymos 是主星，直径 151 米的 Dimorphos 则绕着它运行。2022 年 9 月 26 日，NASA DART 探测器直接撞上较小的 Dimorphos，再测量它绕行主星 Didymos 的时间改变了多少。为了进一步了解这次撞击的影响，Hera 于 2024 年 10 月 7 日发射，历经两年飞行抵达这对小行星附近。它将近距离调查撞击如何改变小行星的轨道与地表，评估这种方法将来能否用来使威胁地球的小行星偏离原有轨道。Hera 用单色小行星取景相机从 60 公里外拍下照片。较小的 Dimorphos 大部分隐没在阴影中，主星 Didymos 则清晰可见。赫拉号拍到的是主星的另一面，地貌与 DART 相机在撞击前不久拍到的那一面明显不同。这一面仍可见先前观测到的赤道隆脊，其余区域则有多块巨石、数个撞击坑，以及疑似沟槽或隆脊的地形。估计已有大量撞击喷出物从较小的 Dimorphos 飞越约 1 公里，抵达主星 Didymos，部分地表特征可能因此形成。Hera 接下来将进一步观察两个天体，有系统地绘制所辨识出的各项变化，并厘清这些地貌是否与喷出物有关。

item.title: 波兰克拉科夫枪击案致6死15伤
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

波兰第二大城市克拉科夫11月7日下午发生严重枪击事件，一名男子驾车闯入市中心历史广场，向人群开枪，造成至少6人死亡、15人受伤，其中包括两名警察。

据美联社及波兰当地媒体报道，枪击发生在当地时间下午3时左右。枪手驾驶汽车进入游客众多的中央集市广场，向周围民众随机射击。警方证实，6名死者包括4名女性和2名男性，另有12名伤者情况危急。

警方表示，嫌疑人为一名24岁的波兰男子，身穿军用风格服装及防弹背心，使用军用类型长枪。警员赶到后与其交火，将其击伤并拘捕。警方还在嫌疑人汽车内发现其他武器及弹药。

警方初步判断枪手单独行动，作案动机及枪支来源仍在调查。

波兰总理图斯克表示，正持续了解事件进展。总统纳夫罗茨基向遇难者家属表示慰问。当地政府已加强现场安全措施，警方表示目前没有发现持续威胁。

关键词: 
波兰
栏目: 
要闻

item.title: 民主党公布新国会优先议程
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

美国民主党在中期选举赢得国会参众两院控制权后，开始制定2027年初的立法议程，计划优先推动扩大医疗保障、恢复医疗保险补贴、结束伊朗战争及调整川普政府的关税政策，同时准备加强对人工智能和数据中心的监管。

据美联社11月7日报道，民主党预计在435席的众议院拥有超过250席。众议院民主党领袖杰弗里斯表示，新国会明年1月3日就职后，将迅速采取行动，把降低民众生活成本作为主要目标。

医疗政策将成为首批立法重点。民主党计划恢复《平价医疗法案》加强型保费税收补贴，并撤销共和党去年通过的医疗补助计划（Medicaid）削减措施。相关削减预计十年内超过9000亿美元，部分措施尚未生效。根据医疗政策研究机构KFF的数据，自2025年7月相关法案签署以来，Medicaid参保人数已减少约500万人。

外交政策方面，民主党计划再次推动限制总统对伊朗军事行动的战争权力法案，并寻求撤销川普政府部分关税措施。此前，国会已多次就伊朗战争权力问题进行表决，但未能有效限制白宫行动。

民主党还成立五个工作组，研究住房、能源、食品及照护等领域的降成本措施。加州民主党众议员刘云平表示，新国会将针对人工智能和数据中心举行公开听证，并推动相关监管立法。目前具体法案内容尚未确定。

不过，民主党虽然掌握两院多数，仍面临立法障碍。参议院一般立法通常需要60票才能结束冗长辩论，而民主党并未取得这一席位数量。即使法案通过两院，川普仍可行使总统否决权。川普在选举当晚已通过社交媒体发布带有“否决”字样的图片。

参议院共和党领袖图恩警告，民主党控制国会可能造成未来两年的政治僵局。参议院民主党领袖舒默则表示，将继续推动议程，并寻求部分共和党议员支持恢复医疗保险补贴。

民主党内部对是否废除参议院冗长辩论规则也存在分歧。部分进步派要求采取更激进的改革措施，但舒默尚未明确承诺修改相关规则。

因此，民主党能够在新一届众议院推动大量法案，却不能保证这些法案最终成为法律。新国会的首批表决将显示两党在医疗、贸易、伊朗战争及人工智能监管等问题上的具体分歧。

item.title: 伊朗宣布取消导弹射程限制
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队11月7日宣布，取消此前自行设定的弹道导弹射程上限，不再将导弹射程限制在2000公里以内。此举发生在美伊军事对抗持续、美国进一步扩大对伊朗封锁之际。

据美联社报道，革命卫队发言人侯赛因·莫赫比在德黑兰记者会上表示，伊朗已经取消这一限制，并称伊朗将通过实际行动展示相关能力，而非仅仅发表声明。

伊朗最高领袖穆杰塔巴·哈梅内伊此前警告，美国或以色列的任何威胁，都可能遭到不受地理范围限制的回应。

伊朗过去宣称自愿将弹道导弹射程限制在2000公里以内，但这并非国际条约规定的限制。该射程已足以覆盖以色列、阿拉伯半岛大部分地区，以及欧洲东南部部分地区。

目前尚无可靠公开证据表明伊朗已经部署射程超过2000公里的弹道导弹。美国官员此前警告，伊朗航天计划使用的部分技术可能被用于发展洲际弹道导弹。

此次宣布意味着伊朗公开放弃原有射程政策，但其实际远程打击能力是否发生变化，仍有待证实。

关键词: 
伊朗

item.title: Trump ally Laura Loomer reportedly charged up to $5,000 for political posts
item.description:
The right-wing activist Laura Loomer has been paid by private clients to make political posts on social media without publicly disclosing the payments, according to a former campaign aide to President Donald Trump and three others familiar with the arrangements, shedding light on what they say is a business practice of one of the Trump administration's most influential online firebrands.

The allegations were made by Alex Bruesewitz, an adviser to Trump's 2024 campaign, and three other people who spoke on the condition of anonymity. Two of the three people said they had paid Loomer directly to post political messages on her X account, where she has 1.9 million followers. The third said they had overseen clients who paid her to post on the account. The three spoke on the condition of anonymity.

Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post.

Bank transaction emails and a wire transfer statement reviewed by The Washington Post appear to show four payments totaling more than $60,000 sent to Loomer and a Florida-based company registered in her name, King Breaker Media, since May of last year.

The documents do not specify the purpose of the payments, but two people familiar with the arrangements said they were for political posts.

Loomer, one of Trump's best-known online acolytes, denied to The Post that she is paid to post on social media. She instead described herself as a journalist and activist and disputed the idea that she is an influencer paid to promote any political cause.

The new claims about Loomer's influence business could add fuel to a growing debate about the little-regulated industry of political messaging on social media, where influencers on both sides of the aisle have operated in a legal gray area between advocacy and advertising.

Bruesewitz first posted his allegations on X on Thursday. Many of the details about Loomer's alleged online influence operation have not been previously reported.

Bruesewitz said in an interview with The Post that he had paid Loomer for tweets last year. He said the money had been sent through his political consulting firm, X Strategies, for posts related to policy issues. He declined to specify what clients.

Despite brokering these deals himself, he believes that they should require clearer disclosures and have "gotten out of hand."

Loomer disputed Bruesewitz's account and said that his firm contacted her last year offering to pay her for research.

"He paid me to make a one-page research document for him, and then he wanted me to distribute the information. And that's what I did," Loomer said. Asked where she was expected to distribute the research, she said, "Either X or maybe an article."

When asked how that was different from being paid to tweet, Loomer said she had actually been told to create the research document but that Bruesewitz had said he would have it distributed.

Loomer accused Bruesewitz of "lashing out" at her because of her political beliefs.

Bruesewitz and the three other people declined to publicly share the tweets they said Loomer had published to maintain the privacy of their clients. But The Post reviewed a selection of the tweets under the condition that they not be revealed publicly.

Two of the people said that Loomer charges $3,000 to $5,000 per tweet, and sometimes more.

Loomer said she does not have set pricing for consulting work. "I certainly don't charge $5,000 for a tweet," she said.

The four people who had paid or oversaw payments to Loomer for posting political statements on social media said she is an effective, if sometimes unpredictable, messenger and a key way of trying to get a line directly to Trump.

Jared Holt, a senior researcher at Open Measures, a platform that measures the spread of online extremism and disinformation, agreed. "This is somebody that has a tremendous amount of influence and access to the president's ear," said Holt, who studies the far right.

Loomer said in an interview Thursday night that she could not discuss the terms of her work with most of her clients due to confidentiality agreements and the fact that her accountant handled her invoices.

"I'm not some influencer that makes money from tweeting. My business is public affairs and opposition research," she said. "I also have a media company. It's not illegal to make a living in America."

Roughly one hour after The Post discussed the claims with Loomer, she announced on X that she is taking a hiatus from her online show, "Loomer Unleashed," so she could pursue a more "healthy work life balance" and prepare for her upcoming wedding.

"I just need to step back, recharge, refocus, and be present in my own life and my own mind with peace and clarity for a little while," she wrote. Loomer said the announcement had been scheduled in advance.

Loomer, 33, has traveled with Trump and met privately with him in the Oval Office during his second term in office. Detractors within the administration have taken issue with Loomer's relationship to the president and have lamented that several high-ranking defense and national security officials have been dismissed after she has publicly rebuked them, often on her X account.

Trump last year called Loomer a "very nice person" and a "patriot." After the White House fired aides on the National Security Council staff last year whom Loomer had accused of disloyalty, Trump denied that she was involved in the dismissal but acknowledged she had made some firing recommendations and said, "Sometimes I listen to those recommendations."

The White House declined to comment.

The Federal Trade Commission requires bloggers, influencers and other online figures to disclose when they have been paid to endorse a product, but the agency doesn't have jurisdiction over political ads.

Some advocacy groups have called for stronger regulations around paid political content. The Campaign Legal Center last year petitioned the Federal Election Commission to consider requiring "paid for by" disclosures on influencers' political posts, saying they could help voters better assess the content they see online. California Gov. Gavin Newsom recently signed legislation that will penalize influencers who post paid political messages without disclosure.

The general lack of transparency among political influencers, Holt said, "further degrades confidence in what people see online and how genuine it may be, or how representative it may actually be of the communities that these various influencers purport to speak for."

Loomer has frequently said her bulldog advocacy reflects her genuine views, telling The Bulwark in May 2025 that she was "not paid for [her] posts."

One person who said they had paid Loomer to tweet on behalf of clients said she was deliberate in her work and would only tweet if she agreed with the position. The person said not every client wanted to work with her because they believed she was polarizing but that some had hired her assuming she had an audience in the White House.

The person added, however, that Loomer was like a "nuclear bomb." "You have to be careful how to use that," they said. "It's effective but also turns a lot of things to s--- if you're not careful."

Loomer said she took that as a compliment. "I'm glad people find me to be effective and think I have a good reach," she said. "I'm not going to apologize for monetizing the fact that people fear me."

Related Content

item.title: Expanding on naval blockade, U.S. military looks to restrict Iranian land commerce
item.description:
(Adds dropped word in paragraph 12)

By Phil Stewart

WASHINGTON, Nov 7 (Reuters) - Building on a months-long naval blockade on Iran, the US military said on Saturday it is launching a task force to help crack ‌down on Tehran's movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material over its land borders and through the ‌Caspian Sea.

Task Force Iron Gate, which was first reported by Reuters, will be based in Tampa, Florida, and will coordinate with other US government agencies. ​Beyond movement of weapons, it will also focus on halting the flow of dual-use technologies used by Iran and stemming what Washington calls illegal revenue streams.

The establishment of the task force is the latest illustration of how the US is still searching for ways to increase pressure on Tehran, more than eight months after launching with Israel a war against the Islamic Republic.

While US ‌strikes have dealt devastating blows to Iran's conventional ⁠military and the US naval blockade has severely restricted its crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz and the Arabian Sea, Iran still poses a formidable threat to the region and its ⁠rulers have tightened their grip on the country.

IRAN'S SECRET NETWORK

A Reuters investigation found Iran has created a secret network of military agencies to import at least $2 billion in hardware, explosives and heavy-duty trucks since January 2025, evading both the US naval blockade and Western ​sanctions.

The ​material entered Iran by cargo ship across the Caspian Sea from ​Russia, by truck from Central Asia, and by freight ‌planes from China, the Reuters investigation showed.

US Central Command said the task force will coordinate with other government agencies. A US military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said that was expected to include the Treasury, State and Justice Departments but also the intelligence community.

"Strengthening CENTCOM’s collaboration with US interagency partners will further constrain Iran’s ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military," Admiral Brad Cooper, the commander of Central Command, said in a statement.

Central Command estimated that its ‌naval blockade has prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion in ​crude oil.

Still, Iran has proven resilient and gloated following US midterm election ​results that punished Trump's Republican Party, giving control of ​Congress to opposition Democrats. Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for electoral rout, and ‌appeared to question whether the conflict was worth it.

Mediators ​have intensified efforts in recent ​days to end the war between Iran and the United States amid fears it could reignite after the US midterm elections.

Trump has been threatening to carry out a new offensive against Iran, putting countries in the Gulf ​on edge, since Tehran has threatened broad ‌retaliation against Gulf infrastructure.

Reuters has reported that US intelligence assessments in recent months have indicated that renewed strikes ​on Iran would not fundamentally change Tehran's negotiating position or lead to the fall of Iran's government.

(Reporting ​by Phil Stewart; Editing by Andrew Heavens and Tomasz Janowski)

This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/exclusive-expanding-naval-blockade-us-133922238.html

item.title: Judge wants to know if Trump officials lied about plans for his D.C. golf course
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A federal judge said Saturday she intends to appoint an ex-top federal prosecutor in the nation's capital during President Donald Trump's first term to investigate whether she was purposefully misled by lawyers and administration officials in a lawsuit challenging one of his prized Washington construction projects, the renovation of a historic public golf course along the Potomac River.

Jessie Liu, a former U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, would examine whether officials with the Interior Department and the National Park Service and attorneys with the Department of Justice violated ethics or misled U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes during the course of the case that was initiated in February by the DC Preservation League and two golfers.

The Republican administration plans to close the East Potomac Golf Course and park on Nov. 15 with the intention of constructing a “World Class, championship-level golf course that is capable of hosting major events." An injunction issued by Reyes last month temporarily bars the government from removing or damaging any additional trees on the course and the administration must give 10 days’ notice in writing before making any “irreparable modification” to any “forms or features” of the course while the lawsuit is active.

Reyes is giving each side a chance to be heard on her plan to name Liu as special master in the case. They must do so in writing by Friday, when the next court hearing in the dispute is scheduled.

Reyes, who was nominated by Democratic President Joe Biden, wants to know whether federal officials lied about the extent of renovation plans during months of hearings. She also wants to know if they were truthful about various steps they took, including cutting hundreds of trees early last month. She announced during a hearing Oct. 30 that she was starting a formal investigation of the government's conduct. Earlier in the case, she had rejected numerous motions from the plaintiffs to step in, saying she trusted the government attorneys.

As the city's chief federal prosecutor, Liu oversaw some of the matters referred to her office by then-special counsel Robert Mueller during his investigation into possible ties between Trump’s 2016 campaign and Russia. Trump later nominated her to be associate attorney general, the third-highest ranking Justice Department job.

Liu withdrew from consideration after running into opposition on the Republican-led Senate Judiciary Committee because of her past membership in a lawyers’ group that has supported abortion rights. She eventually resigned from the group because, she said previously, it took left-leaning positions, and she is now part of her own law firm, Liu Shur Kravis LLP.

David Super, a law professor at the Georgetown University Law Center, said the initiation of a formal investigation by a judge to look into the conduct of a trial's participants "can be a precursor to holding someone in contempt of court.”

Super said it also is a reflection “of the difficulty she had in determining who initiated the tree-cutting in defiance of the assurances DOJ provided. She doesn’t have the time to keep holding long, complex hearings and so wants a special master to narrow the issues.”

Reyes ordered the Oct. 30 hearing after multiple Truth Social posts by Trump indicated there were plans for the golf course and construction was expected to begin Nov. 15. Trump said the park would be closed for 15 months while work goes on.

The presidential posts, which began Oct. 18, created a tense dynamic in multiple court hearings afterward when administration officials could not confirm the existence of the plans under questioning from Reyes. She eventually asked whom she should trust. The Justice Department filed notice Oct. 28 that the plans were real.

___

Bedayn reported from Austin, Texas.

This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/judge-wants-former-us-attorney-174249261.html

item.title: 美批准芯片买家背景遭质疑
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

《纽约时报》11月7日发表调查报道指出，美国川普政府批准多家中国企业购买或组装英伟达H200人工智能芯片，但其中两家企业的登记办公地点缺乏实际运营迹象，另有部分获批企业与美国贸易黑名单上的公司或中国军事供应商存在关联，引发对出口许可审查有效性的质疑。

报道指出，成立约17个月的中国企业新矩阵（New Matrix），今年获得美国商务部许可，将H200芯片组装成人工智能计算机。然而，记者前往该公司在北京的登记地址，发现办公室空置，现场没有公司标识，物业管理人员也表示没有该公司的记录。截至11月6日，该公司网站没有列出员工、招聘职位或发展历史。

中国工商登记资料显示，新矩阵部分股东与中国私募股权基金智路资本及其创办人李斌存在关联。美国商务部2024年将智路资本列入实体清单，指其协助中国政府收购具有战略重要性的半导体企业。两名研究相关企业资料的分析人士认为，新矩阵可能是与智路资本有关的掩护公司，但这一判断尚未得到证实。

另一家获准处理H200芯片的企业麦格纳科技（Maginfra），今年9月也曾受到《纽约时报》调查。记者发现，其登记办公室上锁，内部仅有少量空置家具，工作人员表示从未见过有人在那里办公。

调查发现，麦格纳科技与中国服务器制造商浪潮存在部分人员及专利关联。浪潮此前因涉及中国军事相关活动被美国列入实体清单。

此外，获批企业浙江银盾云科技与曾向中国军事承包商提供云计算服务的企业存在联系；上海嘉唐则与具有军工技术背景的国有企业大唐电信存在历史关联。

美国商务部据报已批准约24家中国企业购买或处理H200芯片，包括百度、比亚迪及特斯拉上海等。川普政府2025年12月决定放宽部分出口限制，允许符合条件的中国客户取得H200芯片，但要求经过美国监管审查，并采取相应安全措施。

曾在川普第一任期及拜登政府担任白宫国家安全委员会中国事务主任的托宾质疑，美国商务部和英伟达是否充分调查相关企业背景，以确保芯片不会流向受限制实体。

美国商务部工业与安全局回应称，所有出口许可申请均经过国家安全风险审查，并表示已增加执法人员，加强出口管制监督。

英伟达发言人则表示，中国政府已严格限制H200进口，以支持本土芯片产业。公司认为，有限度的对华芯片销售仍有助于美国就业和制造业。

《纽约时报》强调，目前没有证据证明上述企业已将H200芯片转交中国军方。不过，登记地点缺乏经营迹象，以及获批企业与受限制实体之间的关联，已使美国现行出口许可和最终用户核查机制受到进一步审视。

芯片

item.title: Races yet to be called: Dems lead Mississippi, Alaska and Colorado
item.description:
Democrats continue to celebrate one of the most lopsided midterm election victories in modern U.S. history, routing their Republican rivals to gain control of the U.S. House, U.S. Senate and statehouses across the country.

In the Senate, Democrats flipped seven seats and now hold 54 to the Republican Party's 44. Two seats — nail-biting contests in Alaska and Mississippi — remain undeclared.

In the House, Democrats held 254 seats to the GOP’s 162 as of Saturday morning, comfortably passing the majority threshold of 218, with 19 races yet to be called, according to the Associated Press. The latest estimates show that the party is on track to win its largest majority since 2008. And there are still seats it could flip, including Colorado’s Fourth District, where Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert, a staunch Trump ally, trails Democrat Eileen Laubacher by about 3,200 votes with 97% of the vote counted, according to the AP.

There were also gubernatorial races, mayoral contests, ballot measures — and plenty of firsts. Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms of Georgia became the first Black woman elected governor in U.S. history, while Democrat Amy Acton became the first woman elected governor of Ohio. In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds became the state's first Black governor-elect. El-Sayed will be America's first Muslim senator.

In a big post-election shake-up, President Trump on Friday announced that Stephen Miller, a top deputy widely viewed as one of the most influential figures behind the administration's agenda, is replacing Susie Wiles as his chief of staff. Miller said he was "honored beyond words" to serve in his new role.

Earlier this week, Trump signaled he would work with Democrats during his remaining two years in office but said he wouldn't hesitate to use his veto power. Trump also acknowledged that the Iran war contributed to Republican losses, but defended his decision to pursue the conflict. "If I had to do it again, I'd have to do it again," he said, adding: "You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon."

Vice President JD Vance, though, blamed the scale of GOP losses squarely on the war with Iran.

"The real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone," he wrote in a post on X. "The reason we lost is the war."

item.title: 埃博拉:英国医生刚果(金)确诊
item.description: 在非洲中部，埃博拉本迪布焦型病毒（Ebola Bundibugyo）疫情自大约半年前（2026年5月中旬）在刚果民主共和国（RD Congo）东部地区爆发以来，现已夺去超过5300人的生命。在刚果（金）疫区内的北基伍省（Nord Kivu）大城市贝尼（Béni），一名参加对抗疫情的英国医生因埃博拉病毒检测呈阳性而于两天前的11月05日星期四被送回国接受治疗。患者目前身体状态稳定，这是本台法国国际广播电台非洲组（RFI Afrique）11月07日星期六的最新法文消息之一。未来几周内，将有两款具针对性的候选疫苗在刚果（金）国内进行临床试验。初步结果预计将于明年（2027年）初揭晓。

item.title: 临近阿布扎比美俄乌会谈 俄罗斯持续袭击乌克兰
item.description: 乌克兰官员周六11月7日表示，俄军在周五到周六的夜间对乌克兰首都基辅及周边地区发动导弹与无人机攻击，造成1死8伤，伤者包括1名儿童，除了住宅及非住宅建筑受到迫害外，还造成能源基础设施及一座横跨第聂伯河（Dnipro River）的重要桥梁毁损。

item.title: 特朗普公开邀请UFC总裁出任白宫新闻发言人
item.description: 美国总统特朗普近日公开向终极格斗冠军赛（UFC）总裁达纳·怀特（Dana White）抛出橄榄枝，邀请其出任白宫新闻发言人一职，美国总统在其社交媒体平台Truth Social上发布了这一消息，并特别指出怀特尚未接受邀请。他写道：“达纳，请接受这份工作。”
